correctness.rationale: For a word of least period a, the pointwise sieve sums mu(n/d) over a|d|n, giving 1 exactly when a=n. Transforming the subgroup indicators gives exactly q^d on their annihilators under counting normalization. Nonzero Möbius coefficients force b|d, so characters outside V_b^perp receive no terms. Inside it the b-term is present and the largest surviving signed power strictly dominates all smaller distinct powers, including q=2. Divisibility gives the lower bound q^b; placing a nontrivial character and its inverse at 0 and b kills the restriction only at V_b among active block divisors, attaining the bound. This works even for order-two characters and n=2. The trivial character attains the largest multiplier by triangle inequality. Fourier diagonalization and double annihilation give rank, nullity, stabilizer and range; averaging is a contraction fixing constants. The sample ranks agree. At line 29, 'squarefree kernel b' should read 'n divided by the squarefree radical'; b itself need not be squarefree. The displayed definitions and theorems are unambiguous.
residual_risks: The finite checks are corroboration only; no formal proof-assistant or expert attestation is asserted.
